Singh, J.K. and Rout, A.K. (2018). Advances in Green Steel Making Technology - A Review. American Journal of Materials Engineering and Technology 6(1), 8-13. doi:10.12691/materials-6-1-2

background: Short descriptive review (6 pages) of PCI, continuous casting, coke dry quenching and CCS with no sourced technology-level tables; a few generic figures without attribution, no costs (other than a payback range), no capacity-normalised energy use for any archetype. What it has: PCI maximum about 0.27 t coal/t HM and coke 286-320 kg/t HM at 170-200 kg PCI (modern BF); coke dry quenching steam 500-700 kg/t coke and power 140-185 kWh/t coke, payback 3-5 years, 15-18 MW from a CDQ plant over 100 t/h; integrated-mill GHG source shares (BF stove 43%, misc. combustion 30%, other units 15%, electricity 12%). Locators are printed journal pages 8-13.
